Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Health | National Gender Ministry rolls out free breast and medical screening for Civil Service Staff Source : Myjoyonline.com 22 October 2026 5:09pm Audio By Carbonatix
The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MoGCSP) has commenced a free breast and medical screening exercise for Civil Service staff as part of activities marking Breast Cancer Awareness Month 2026.
The exercise, running from October 19 to 28 at the Ministry’s old office building, offers breast screening, blood pressure and blood sugar checks, general medical consultations and health education to promote preventive healthcare and encourage early detection of diseases.
In an address delivered on behalf of the Chief Director, Dr Marian Kpakpah, a Principal Programme Officer at the Department of Gender, Sabia Kpekata said the initiative reflected the Ministry’s commitment to safeguarding the health and well-being of its workforce.
She said the exercise was intended to encourage early detection, timely diagnosis and access to appropriate medical care.
Madam Kpekata stressed that breast cancer awareness should go beyond public campaigns and translate into practical action, including seeking reliable health information, paying attention to changes in the body and consulting qualified health professionals when necessary.
She urged staff to take advantage of the free screening services and make their health a priority.
She also highlighted the need for compassion and support for people affected by breast cancer, noting that the disease can affect not only individuals but also their families, livelihoods and emotional well-being.
Madam Kpekata called for greater understanding and an end to stigma and discrimination against people living with the disease.
Held under the theme, “ Every Story is Unique, Every Journey Matters ,” the initiative reinforces the importance of early detection, timely medical attention and collective responsibility in improving health outcomes.
